name: contact-section
title: Contact Section
description: A slim bordered contact block with corner crosshair marks: a Get in touch header, phone and email rows, then a Send a message form with name, email, phone, message and a full-width Submit button.
use: A marketing or studio site wants a compact contact block that pairs direct phone and email details with a message form.
avoid: It must actually send: Submit is a plain button and there is no validation, action or success state.
a11y: Labels are tied to their inputs and the decorative marks are hidden, but Submit does not submit and there is no error messaging. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A narrow dark panel in a thin border, with small plus marks at its corners. The top holds the Get in touch heading, two grey lines and phone and email rows with outline icons. Below a divider, first and last name sit in two columns, then stacked email, phone and a tall message box, ending in a white full-width Submit.
behaves: Static: the fields take focus and text with standard focus rings and the rows react to hover, but nothing moves and Submit is a button that does not send the form.
customise: Phone, email, headings and form fields are written into the component, so changing them needs a source edit; the corner marks and border are fixed decoration.
weight: light: A static bordered form with a handful of inputs; nothing animates or polls.
demo: Get in touch; phone +1 (555) 123-4567 and email hello@northwind.studio; fields prefilled with Maya Okafor.
issues: Submit is a plain type-button control, so the form never sends anything.
The first and last name row stays two columns even on very narrow screens.
polishWhy: Clean orderly form with a neat corner detail; default fields and a dead Submit keep it ordinary.
